title: Orchestrator–Workers
brief: Three research questions come in, and each one really has four parts. A single agent searches them one by one: its context fills with raw pages, it runs out of patience, and about two answers in three cover only some of the parts. Make a lead agent plan the split and hand each part to its own worker. Get at least 85% complete reports while the lead's context stays under 12,000 tokens.

data.systemPrompt: Research the question thoroughly and write a cited report.

data.name: web_search
data.description: Searches the web and returns the top 5 pages as text.

data.systemPrompt: You are the lead researcher. Split the question into 4 independent parts, give each to a worker with a clear brief, then merge their findings into one cited report.

data.name: web_search
data.description: Searches the web and returns the top 5 pages as text.

data.name: run_worker
data.description: Starts a worker agent on one part of the question with its own brief and returns its findings with sources.

tasks.label: Heat pump market
tasks.prompt: Should we enter the German residential heat pump market in 2027? Cover demand, subsidies, installer capacity and competitors.

tasks.label: Vector database choice
tasks.prompt: Compare three hosted vector databases for 50M embeddings: cost, latency, filtering and data residency.

tasks.label: Drug interaction review
tasks.prompt: Summarize the evidence on combining metformin with GLP-1 agonists: efficacy, side effects, dosing and open trials.

search.text: web_search("part 2 of 4: subsidies 2027") (lead reads 5 full pages itself)

partial.text: Report: detailed sections on the first two parts. The last two parts get one line each: 'more research needed'.

solo_full.text: Report: all four parts covered, 14 sources (after a long single-threaded search).

plan.text: Plan: 4 independent parts. Worker briefs: (1) demand, (2) subsidies, (3) installer capacity, (4) competitors. Each: search, read, return a 300-word brief with sources and open questions. No overlap.

dispatch.text: run_worker ×4 in parallel, one brief per part

merge_ok.text: Report: four sections from four worker briefs, merged and cross-checked, 23 sources, two open questions flagged.

merge_gap.text: Report: merged the four briefs, but two workers searched the same thing and part 3 is missing. The lead did not notice.

modifiers.note: After a few searches the single agent wants to wrap up, often before every part is covered.
With workers available, the lead delegates instead of searching itself.
Without separate worker contexts, 16k tokens of raw pages land in the lead and the merge gets sloppy.

hints: Read a failing report. Which parts got skipped, and how big was the lead's context by then?
Give the lead a run_worker tool and a planning prompt, so it splits the question into parts and hands them out instead of searching itself.
Workers need their own context windows: wire a Subagent node to run_worker, and turn on Parallel tool calls so the four workers run at once.
explain: The lead does the two things only it can do, splitting and merging, and each worker spends a fresh context on one part. Four workers read four times as much, and the lead only sees their briefs.
